pages.text: After rain, the ground under the tree was soggy. Sitting there made their bottoms wet. Taro and Mumu looked at the damp soil.
"Let's bring a big stone!" "We can sit on it." They went to find one.
Taro imagined a stone as big as his palm. Mumu imagined one big enough to sit on. Both called it a big stone.
Taro found a stone in the stream. It fitted snugly in his hand. "This is big enough!"
Mumu found a roadside stone. It was too heavy to lift, so Mumu rolled it along.
Taro put his stone under the tree. "All done!" He tried sitting on it.
His bottom did not fit, and his feet were still in the soggy ground. Taro tilted his head.
Mumu rolled up with the big stone. Rumble, rumble. Taro's eyes widened. "That's your big stone?"
They pushed together. Heave-ho! They rolled it all the way under the tree.
They sat side by side on the big stone, with dry bottoms. Taro's little stone became a footrest.
